title: An Empirical Refutation of Yajnadevam's Devanagari-Based Decipherment of the Indus Script
summary: An empirical and computational critique of the proposed Devanagari-based decipherment of the Indus script by Yajnadevam. By analyzing the structural characteristics of the Sanskrit language in Devanagari and comparing it with the transitional probabilities, sign distribution frequencies, and positional patterns of the Indus sign corpus, we show a systematic and mathematically provable divergence. The mapping is demonstrated to be statistically unviable and structurally inconsistent.
